set-screw-tip-selection:
Compare the four contact mechanisms

Set-screw point selection: geometry and trade-offs
Point formContactWhen to review itWhat to verify
Flat pointA broad end face bears against a prepared flat or pad.Review for adjustments where a sharp biting edge is undesirable.It can still mark the mating surface. Check flat alignment, contact pressure and retention.
Cone pointA pointed end engages a suitable recess or indents the mating surface.Review for a defined setting where penetration or a mating recess is acceptable.Repeated relocation can damage the contact area. Define the cone and the mating feature.
Dog pointA cylindrical extension enters a prepared hole or slot.Review when the extension must locate or guide a component.Specify projection, diameter, clearance and available depth; do not let the point bottom unintentionally.
Cup pointThe rim of a recessed end makes concentrated contact.Review for a setting where an indentation is acceptable.Do not assume an undamaged surface after removal, or infer a universal holding force from the point name.

Compare the contact mechanism first; confirm capacity and installation on the actual joint.
